# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - After two weeks of trading in 2012, gold, silver and platinum are comfortably above where they started the year in price terms while palladium is the only metal to exhibit marked weakness. Gold seems to have benefited from its safe haven status, rising even as the Euro weakened, assisted by strong Chinese buying. Movements in the silver price were rather limited by recent standards as it followed the yellow metal. Platinum benefited from (excessive) worries over South African electricity supply and from healthy buying by the Chinese jewellery industry, moving above $1,500 briefly. In the last week, the platinum-gold spread has moved in platinum’s favour, falling from a high of $215 to its current $150. Palladium weakened: it does not experience the same seasonal demand in China as platinum and gold and investors showed little inclination to join the market just yet. However, ETF flows in palladium did reverse, with fresh purchasing helping to reassure the shorter term bulls. - Net long speculative positioning on the futures exchanges increased for three of the precious metals in the week to the 10th of January. Sentiment seemed positive towards the complex in general, although positions are small by recent standards. Palladium saw net long speculative positioning fall below half a million ounces for the first time since 2008 as the price declined towards $610. • All four major precious metals (although not rhodium) recorded net inflows of metal into their Exchange Traded Funds in the week to the 13th of January. Sentiment was almost uniformly favourable on gold but less convincingly positive for the other metals. Palladium ETFs recorded net additions of metal for the first time in ten weeks and it will be interesting to see if sentiment remains positive. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **16 January 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **16 January 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 10 January 2012; ETF data to 13 January 2012.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Sentiment remains bullish across the market despite concerns over Europe weakening the Euro. Strong buying interest in China outweighed Indian price sensitivity and provided further support for the price. The decision by Standard & Poor’s to downgrade a range of European sovereign debt ratings on Friday the 13th has applied further pressure on the Euro, weighing on the precious metals. Gold is now faced with a choice as to whether to reassert its safe haven credentials. Signs of ETF buying suggest that it may do this and move up from its current $1,640. However, physical flows into China are likely to weaken in the remaining days before Chinese New Year (the 23rd of January this year) and any appreciation in price will be hard-won. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Jan 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Net long speculative interest on COMEX declined from 25 million ounces in mid-November to 16.8 million ounces at the end of 2011. In the following week, however, they rebounded by 660,000 ounces. TOCOM investors were bullish too, adding to their positions. - Apart from roughly one tonne of redemptions from the SPDR ETF, sentiment was very positive towards gold from ETF investors in the week to the 13th of January. Most of the funds which we monitor reported net inflows of metal. Overall, 428,000 ounces of metal were bought, bringing to an end four weeks of net selling. Total positions

stand at 69.3 million ounces. We expect to see more buying this week. 2 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **16 January 2012** ### **Silver CFTC data to 10 January 2012; ETF data to 13 January 2012.** ## **Exchange (COMEX) and ETF Silver Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

- In the first two weeks of 2012, silver has traded in a range of little over $2.50. While this is wide in historical terms, it is certainly not excessive compared to last year’s gyrations in the price. There currently seems to be little excitement in this market and silver has been driven by movements in the Dollar and in the gold price. The gold:silver ratio has moved between 54 and 56.2. The two major price moves came on the 3rd and the 10th when silver climbed roughly a Dollar. From the 10th onwards, silver has flirted with the $30 target and remained relatively robust considering the weakness of the Euro. Given the numerous credit ratings downgrades of European sovereign debt on Friday, any successful attempt to challenge $30 would be positive. - Net long speculative interest in silver on COMEX increased by 14 million ounces to 116 million ounces, having climbed by 9.9 million ounces in the previous week. However, on this occasion, open interest declined and it was short covering rather than the opening of fresh long interest that was responsible for the increase in net positioning. Sentiment remains rather muted t

owards silver from investors with a determined move of the price in one direction or another probably needed to rekindle interest. - The silver ETFs saw gentle net buying in the week to the 13th of January, after four weeks of net selling. However, only 285,000 ounces were purchased and buying was only seen in the ZKB fund, presenting a less than convincing bullish case. - Price action in platinum illustrated the danger of short exposure to a commodity which is as reliant on supply from one country as platinum. Platinum started the year pushing from $1,400 to $1,430 on the 4th before a weakening Euro dragged prices briefly back below the $1,400 level on the 9th. General sentiment across a range of markets seemed positive, though, and once the Euro stopped softening on the 9th, platinum was able to move higher. News reports confirming the current wafer-thin electricity generating reserves of South Africa’s Eskom applied further pressure, sending platinum quickly to $1,460 on the 10th and triggering short covering. Strong buying on SGE ahead of Chinese New Year added some further energy. The price touched $1,508 on the 12th but has since fallen a little lower on the Europea

n credit rating downgrades and the realisation that there are no actual electricity shortages affecting the platinum mining industry yet. The approach of Chinese New Year means that physical support for the price may be limited in the coming days. - The addition of fresh long positions by larger investors drove net long speculative platinum positions on NYMEX 28,000 ounces higher in the week to the 10th of January. Overall positioning has changed little since the start of December. We expect next week’s data to reveal substantial short covering as one of the reasons for last week’s price move. TOCOM investors also added 13,000 ounces to their net long positioning. - Sentiment from ETF buyers of platinum has turned more positive in the last month with the week to the 13th of January seeing net buying for the second consecutive week and for the third week out of the last four. Buying was not strong but even so, net inflows of 10,000 ounces drove holdings back up to 1.41 million ounces of metal, a positive sign of investor appetite. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **16 January 2012** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 10 January 2012; ETF data to 13 January 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

- Sentiment towards palladium seemed muted in the first two weeks of January 2012. The Euro started the year weakly and dragged palladium prices lower from a high of almost $670 on the 3rd to a low of $608 on the 9th. The Euro finally

stopped in its fall (for the moment at least), allowing palladium to regroup before news reports of tightness in electricity supply drove platinum and palladium higher, with palladium reaching a high of $648 on the 12th. It has since given up some ground to trade at close to $640. 

- Open interest in palladium on NYMEX rose a little in the week to the 10th of January. Investors cut their bullish bets a little but short non-commercial interest rose by over ten per cent, with net positions shortening from a long 534,000 ounces to only 462,000 ounces. The last time positioning was below 500,000 ounces was September 2008 when the price was below $250. Although there is plenty of scope for a bullish move from here, this lack of investor interest is less positive. 

- After nine consecutive weeks of selling from ETF investors, the week to the 13th of January saw net buying of 5,000 ounces. It will be interesting to see if this marks a change in investor sentiment, in which case we can expect a push to higher prices, or if this is simply a one-off event.
